children: Interactive Brokers Group reported a higher profit in the third quarter, as futures trading on the online brokerage platform rose while stock trading fell.
The company on Thursday reported a third-quarter profit of $314 million, or 69 cents a share, compared with a profit of $263 million, or 59 cents a share, a year earlier.
On an adjusted basis, earnings were 67 cents a share, in line with the expectations of analysts polled by FactSet.
Revenue grew to $1.91 billion from $1.66 billion, including a 12% rise in commission revenue to $602 million. Analysts were expecting $1.86 billion in revenue.
Trading volumes were up 13% in futures, but fell 24% in stocks and 1% in options.
Customer equity increased 27% to $964.7 billion. Customer accounts were up 35% at 5.58 million.
Interactive Brokers also raised its quarterly dividend to 15 cents from 8.75 cents.
